summary: The root (lwH) primarily conveys the meaning of appearing, shining, or gleaming, like a star or lightning. It also describes something becoming apparent or manifest.
lane: 1 لَاحَ ذ , aor. يَلُوحُ , inf. n. لَوْحٌ , It (a thing) shone; gleamed; glistened. (S.) -b2- لَاحَ , (aor. يَلُوحُ , inf. n. لَوْحٌ and لُؤُوحٌ and لَوَحَانٌ ; TA;) and ; It (lightning) flashed slightly, not extending sideways in the adjacent tracts of cloud: (S, K:) or signifies it lighted up what surrounded it. (TA.) -b3- لَاحَ , (S, Msb,) aor. يَلُوحُ ; (Msb;) inf. n. [ لَوْحٌ and] لِيَاحٌ ; (IAth;) It appeared: (IAth, Msb:) it (a star) appeared, (S, Msb,) as also , (S, K,) [ it loomed, ] and shone, gleamed, or glistened; (TA;) as also : (Msb, TA:) ISk says, لَاحَ سُهَيْل Canopus appeared; (S;) and it shone and glistened. (S, K.) -b4- لاح , and , He (a man) came forth and became apparent. (A 'Obeyd.) -b5- لَاحَ لِى أَمْرُكَ , and , (tropical:) Thine affair became apparent and manifest to me. (A.) -b6- لَاحَ الشَّيْبُ فِى رَأْسِهِ Hoariness appeared upon his head. (TA.) -b7- لَاحَهُ , aor. يَلُوحُ , He saw him, or it. (K.) -b8- لَاحَ إِلَى كَذَا , aor. يَلُوحُ , He looked at, or towards, such a thing; as a distant fire. (L.) -b9- لَاحَهُ بِبَصَرِهِ , aor. يَلُوحُ , inf. n. لَوْحَةٌ , [so in the L,] He saw him, or it, and then he or it became concealed from him. (L.) -b10- See 4. -A2- لَاحَ , (S,) aor. يَلُوحُ , (TA,) inf. n. لَوْحٌ (S, K,) and لُوحٌ (K) and لُوَاحٌ (S, K) and لُؤُوحٌ and لَوَحَانٌ ; (K;) and ; (S, K;) He thirsted: (S, K;) or he thirsted in the slightest degree: (TA:) or he thirsted quickly. (Lh.) -b2- لَاحَهُ , (aor. يَلُوحُ , inf. n. لَوْحٌ , TA,) It (thirst, K, or travel, S, K, and cold, and disease or illness, and grief, TA,) altered him, (S, K,) and made him lean, lank, light of flesh, slender, or lank in the belly; (TA;) as also , (K,) inf. n. تَلْوِيحٌ : or the latter signifies it (the heat of fire or of the sun) altered the colour of his skin: (TA:) or both verbs signify it parched, scorched, or burned, and blackened, his skin. (Zj.) الشَّمْسُ The sun altered him, and scorched, i. e. slightly burned, and changed the colour of, his face; (S;) and in like manner fire, and the hot wind called سَمُوم ; as also لَاحَتْهُ . (A.)

headwords.def: aor. يَلُوحُ, inf. n. لَوْحٌ, It (a thing) shone; gleamed; glistened. (S.) لَاحَ, (aor. يَلُوحُ, inf. n. لَوْحٌ and لُؤُوحٌ and لَوَحَانٌ; TA;) and; It (lightning) flashed slightly, not extending sideways in the adjacent tracts of cloud: (S, K:) or signifies it lighted up what surrounded it. (TA.) لَاحَ, (S, Msb,) aor. يَلُوحُ; (Msb;) inf. n.
(inf. n. تَلْوِيحٌ, TA,) He heated (S, K) a thing with fire. (S; see MA, and see 1.) لوّحهُ الشَّيْبُ Hoariness altered him; (TA;) rendered him white. (K, TA.) See 1, and 4.

أَلْوَحَ See 1 throughout the first half. الاح مِنَ الشَّىْءِ, (inf. n. الاحة, TA,) (tropical:) He (a man) was cautious and fearful of the thing. (S, K. *) الاح بِثَوْبِهِ, (L,) and به, (Lh, S, L,) and به, (L,) (tropical:) He made a sign with his garment, (S, L,) from a distant place, taking the end of it in his hand, and waving it about, to make it seen by some one whom he desired to see it. (L.) الاح بِسَيْفِهِ; (S, K;) and به, (K,) inf. n.
He sought, tried, or endeavoured, to see, syn. تَبَصَّرَ, (K,) فِى الأَمْرِ into the affair, or thing. (TA.)

A look; syn. نَظْرَةٌ; [or rather a glance, or light or quick look; ] like لَمْحَةٌ. (K.) See لُوحٌ Any broad, or wide, and thin, thing, such as a board or plank or the like, of wood or of bone: (T, M, Msb, K:) pl. أَلْوَاحٌ, and pl. pl. أَلَاوِيحُ. (K.) A word of this kind has not a pl. of the measure أَفْعُلٌ, because dammeh to the و is disliked. (Sb.) أَلْوَاحٌ i. q. لَوَائِحُ, q. v. The scapula or shoulder-blade, (T, S, Msb, K,) when it is written upon, or inscribed.

(S, K) and, (Lh, K,) but the former is of higher authority, (K,) and the latter is mentioned by none but Lh, (TA,) The air, or atmosphere, (S, K,) between heaven and earth: (S:) the air next to the higher part, or to the clouds, of the sky; syn. سُكَاك: this is its meaning in the phrase لَا أَفْعَلُ ٰلِكَ وَلَوْ نَزَوْتَ فِى اللُّوحِ [ I will not do that even if thou leap into the air next to the higher part, or to the clouds, of the sky ]. (S.)

شَىْءٌ لِيَاحٌ , (S, K,) and, (K,) A white thing. (S.) The و is changed into ى because of the kesreh before it. (Fr, S.) لَيَاحٌ is extr.; for there is no reason for the change of the و therein into ى, unless for alleviation of the sound. (L.) Also لِيَاحٌ and Of a shining, or glistening, white hue. (L.) أَبْيَضُ لِيَاحٌ, and, (tropical:) Intensely white. (K, TA.) Also لِيَاحٌ (S, K) and (K) The wild bull: (S, K:) so called because of his whiteness.
لَوَّاحَةٌ لِلْبَشَرِ , [Kur, lxxiv. 29, referring to سَقَرُ,] Burning the [ scarf- ] skin so as to blacken it. (Zj.)

لَوَائِحُ شَىْءٍ [pl. of لَائِحَةٌ ] The parts of a thing that are apparent, and that show the signs thereof. (TA.) لَوَائِحُ and The external parts of a thing. (A.) لَوَاحِى الشَّيْبِ The apparent signs of hoariness, occurs in a verse of Khufáf Ibn-Nudbeh, for لَوَائِح الشيب.

Large in the أَلْوَاح, (K,) meaning [the shoulder-blades, or] any of the wide bones of the body: applied to a camel and to a man: (TA:) or having excellent and large الواح: (Sh, AHeyth:) and الواح is said to mean the ِرَاعَانِ [or two radii ], the سَاقَانِ [or two tibiæ ], and the عَضُدَانِ [or two humeri, or upper bones of the arms ]. (TA.) Tall.

Altered by fire, or by the sun, or by travel, [ &c. ]: an arrow, before it is furnished with feathers and a head, altered by fire; and in like manner the iron head of an arrow or of a spear, or the like: (TA:) also altered (K) by the sun, or by travel, &c. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
